title: Digital footprint
examples: Teacher, if I delete a picture, does it really go away forever?
What are the best ways to keep my personal information safe online?
Why is it important to think before I post something on social media?

explain.say: Your digital footprint is the trail you leave online.
Some things you post online are permanent records.
Think about photos of your friends and family.
Privacy settings control who sees your posts.
You can set your profiles to be private.
In real life, you should think about your words too.

draw.text: Real life: Think before you speak

faq.q: If I delete a post, is it completely gone from the internet?
faq.a: No, even deleted things can sometimes be saved by others or stored on servers. You should assume it might stay online.
asks: Does deleting something make it disappear?
Can people find my old posts even if I delete them?

faq.q: What is the difference between public and private settings?
faq.a: Public means anyone can see it, while private means only people you approve can view it. Always check these settings.
asks: When should I use private settings?

faq.q: Should I share my location when I am out with friends?
faq.a: It is best not to share your exact location in real time. Wait until you are safely home to share pictures.
asks: Is it safe to post where I am right now?
Should I share my travel plans online?

faq.q: Can someone use my name or picture without asking me?
faq.a: Yes, people can sometimes use your information without permission. This is why strong privacy settings are important.
asks: Is it okay for others to use my photos?
What if someone steals my identity online?

faq.q: How often should I check my privacy settings?
faq.a: You should check them regularly, maybe every few months. Online platforms change their settings often.
asks: Do I need to check my settings always?
How often should I update my privacy?

facts: Your digital footprint includes everything you post and every time you search.
Even if you delete content, copies might exist elsewhere online.
Privacy settings let you choose who sees your online activity.
Never share passwords or private personal details with strangers online.

quiz.say: If you post a picture of a school event, and you set it to 'Friends only', who can see it?
quiz.why: This setting limits viewing to people you know and trust.

wrong.0: This is too specific; 'Friends only' is about your contacts, not just your school.
wrong.1: This is too restrictive; 'Friends only' includes more people than just parents.
wrong.2: The administrator can see it, but that is not what 'Friends only' means.

quiz.say: Which action contributes to your digital footprint?

options.show: Talking to a friend face to face
options.say: Talking to a friend face to face

quiz.why: Every search you make leaves a record of what you were curious about.

wrong.0: This is offline communication and does not create a digital record.
wrong.1: A physical diary is not connected to the internet.
wrong.2: Reading a book does not generate online data.

quiz.say: If you want to make sure only people you know can see your posts, which setting should you check?
quiz.why: These settings are the tools you use to control your visibility online.

wrong.0: The 'Like' button is an action, not a control setting.
wrong.1: The 'Share' button lets you send it, but the setting controls the default audience.
wrong.3: The delete button removes the post, but it does not control who saw it before.
